newsitem.title: RUSSIA: FOCUS - Russia plans to sell UES stake with bond.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Russia plans to sell UES stake with bond.

text.p: Russia plans to sell a 7.5 percent stake in national power company UES later this year through an issue of convertible bonds aimed in part at foreign investors, privatisation officials said on Friday.
The State Property Committee said the issue would be split into four parts -- aimed at investors in Europe, North America, Asia and Russia.

A high-powered team of international and foreign advisers, led by CS First Boston as global coordinator, has been assembled to handle the sale, which should bring in a large chunk of the 12 trillion roubles ($2.2 billion) the government is seeking this year from privatisation.
The UES stake, currently in state hands, will be sold through convertible bonds but terms will be fixed by the deal's managers, the Russian Privatisation Centre said.
"It will all be decided during the preparatory period," centre spokeswoman Yelena Shalneva told Reuters.

Unifed Energy System (UES), which owns 29 power plants and holds 49 percent stakes in most of Russia's "energo" regional utilities, is one of Russia's biggest companies by market capitalisation and one of its most liquid shares.
UES shares closed at $0.0768 on the Russian Trading System, down from $0.077. A 7.5 percent stake would be worth some $225 million at current prices.
Under a government resolution, the state is to keep a 51 percent stake in UES until the end of 1998. The state has a further 8.5 percent.
Foreigners own 20 percent of the company and UES President Anatoly Dyakov said last month an increase in the foreign shareholding was inadmissible.
However, Natalya Ivanova of United City Bank said the UES sale was likely to spark investor interest.
"It is good news and it is good that the orientation of this deal is not only for the Russian market but for the foreign market as well," she said.
UES is hugely powerful as the national grid covering most of Russia and it has stakes in all but two of the 72 energos.
"Investment in this company is investment in something which controls the market but it is not like a usual company," she said.

UES said in May it expected to boost its pre-tax profits by a third this year from 622 billion roubles in 1995. Its pre-tax profit in the first quarter of this year was 180 billion, compared with 150 billion a year earlier.
However, the whole industry is mired in a vast payments problem, with many customers not paying their bills.
Tariffs, though set to rise, are low and regulated but many customers have spiralling debts.
In turn, this has caused problems for some energos.

Thousands of power workers in the Far East have been staging strikes for weeks, demanding payment of back wages. Households and industry in Vladivostok are spending large parts of every day without power.
The UES sale via convertibles follows the sale of about nine percent of oil company LUKoil through convertible bonds.

Power generation is one of the sectors which has proved most interesting to foreign investors, who have bought into UES and also into regional companies such as Mosenergo, Irkutskenergo and Lenenergo. ($1=5400 Rouble)
